rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 2] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Michael B. McNaughton. Before the court is Tuyen T. Tran's Motion to Quash Subpoena for Financial Records and Request for Protective Order ("Motion"). No written opposition to the Motion was filed. In the underlying matter, Decedent Robert L. Gaherty died on January 30, 2025. Competing petitions have been filed by Movant, Tuyen T. Tran, seeking to admit to probate a 2021 pour-over will, and by Dena Gaherty, seeking to admit to probate a 2024 will. The petitioners have each filed objections to the other's petition. Ms. Tran also filed a will contest to the 2024 will. The parties were referred to pro bono mediation by order of this court on May 16, 2026. The status hearing on mediation and hearings on the underlying petitions are currently set for September 23, 2026. No one has been appointed personal representative in this matter. Per the Notice of Motion, Movant moves pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 1985.3 and 1987.1 for an order of this court quashing the subpoena for financial records Dena Gaherty caused to be served on Morgan Stanley/E*Trade. The Motion is GRANTED, as follows. The subject Deposition Subpoena for Production of Business Records and Notice to Consumer are attached as part of Exhibit C to the Memorandum of Points and Authorities. Per the face of these documents, they were both issued on April 10, 2026. The Proof of Service section of the Deposition is blank, but the Deposition is signed and dated by counsel as having issued on April 10, 2026, with a production date of May 15, 2026. The Notice to Consumer is also signed and dated by counsel on April 10, 2026. The Proof of Service section of the Notice to Consumer indicates it was served on Ms. Tyran by mail. Under Code of Civil Procedure section 1985.3(b), the consumer whose personal records are sought must be served a copy of the deposition subpoena, the Notice to Consumer form (SUBP-025), and "proof of service as indicated in paragraph (1) of subdivision (c)" of section 1985.3. Service of the required documents on the consumer must occur at least five days prior to service on the custodian of records, and not less than ten days prior to the date of production specified in the subpoena, plus any additional time required for service by mail under Section 1013. (Code of Civil Procedure section 1985.3.) The Notice to Consumer was not served a least five days prior to service on the custodian of records, as required under Section 1985.3(b). Service of the Notice to Consumer is defective pursuant to Section 1985.3, and the Motion to quash service is granted on those grounds. The Motion seeks an order quashing the subpoena, pursuant to Section 1987.1. Movant argues the subject subpoena seeks confidential financial information protected under California privacy law, and that the subpoena is overbroad.

rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 2] A right of privacy does exist as to a party's confidential financial affairs (see, e.g., Fortunato v. Sup. Ct. (2003) 114 Cal. App. 4th 475, 481). "[A] court faced with a motion for protective order should carefully balance "the right of civil litigants to discover relevant facts, on the one hand, with the right of bank customers to maintain reasonable privacy regarding their financial affairs, on the other." (Valley Bank of Nevada v. Superior Ct. (1975) 15 Cal. 3d 652, 656.) Among other considerations, the party seeking discovery of confidential information has the burden of making a threshold showing that the evidence sought is "directly relevant" to the claim or defense. The broad "relevant to the subject matter" standard under Code of Civil Procedure section 2017.010 and Evidence Code section 210 is insufficient. (Harris v. Superior Ct. (1992) 3 Cal. App. 4th 661, 665 (disapproved on other grounds by Williams v. Sup.Ct. (Marshalls of CA, LLC) (2017) 3 C5th 531, 557 & fn. 8); see also, Valley Bank, supra, at p. 658, and Fortunato, supra, at p. 481.) The Attachment No. 3 to the Deposition Subpoena lists an account number ending in XX-208 and states the records subject to the subpoena are, "Any and all documents or online transactions submitted by Tuyen Tran for any and all withdrawals and/or transfers made by her from Mr. Gaherty's account to her or her accounts on or about April 11, 2025." Here, the subpoenaing party has not filed any opposition to the Motion, nor made any showing in response to the Motion that the information sought through the subpoena is "directly relevant" to a claim or defense in this matter or that it is reasonably tailored to lead to the discovery of admissible evidence. With respect to the Motion's request for a protective order, that request is not contained in the Notice of Motion nor is it discussed in Movant's Memorandum of Points and Authorities.
